records.name: Batch-Only Processing
records.definition: Processing data in scheduled batches rather than as a continuous low-latency stream.

records.name: Ordering/State
records.definition: The degree to which processing an unbounded stream complicates preserving event order and bounded state.

records.name: Forward-Only State Model
records.definition: The requirement that processing keep only forward-moving state, never needing to revisit earlier input.

records.name: Global Optimization
records.definition: The degree to which processing data in a single pass forgoes optimizations that need a full view of the data.

records.name: Multi-Pass Full Materialization
records.definition: Loading a full dataset into memory and traversing it in multiple passes, rather than in a single streaming pass.

records.name: Error Propagation/Debugging
records.definition: The degree to which splitting work into pipeline stages makes an error harder to trace back to its origin.

records.name: Monolithic Processing Function
records.definition: One large function that performs every processing step at once, so stages cannot be tested or reused independently.

records.name: Stage Contracts
records.definition: The requirement that each pipeline stage declare a typed contract for what it consumes and produces.

records.name: Stepwise Transformation
records.definition: The ability to transform data through a sequence of small, composable stages.

records.name: Streaming
records.definition: The ability to process data continuously as it arrives rather than in complete batches.

records.name: Avoiding Unneeded Work
records.definition: The ability to skip computing results that are never used.

records.name: Debuggability/Resource Lifetime
records.definition: The degree to which deferring computation makes execution order harder to debug and resource lifetimes harder to reason about.

records.name: Deferred Execution Semantics
records.definition: The requirement that a computation's semantics defer its work until the result is demanded.

records.name: Eager Full Materialization
records.definition: Computing and materializing a complete result up front, rather than deferring computation until parts are needed.

records.name: Large Data Processing
records.definition: The ability to process datasets larger than memory by reading them in order, a piece at a time.

records.name: Lookup Performance
records.definition: The degree to which reading strictly in sequence makes locating a specific item by key slow.

records.name: Ordered Read Model
records.definition: The requirement that data be read in a fixed forward order rather than by arbitrary index.

records.name: Random Access Requirement
records.definition: A need to read arbitrary items by position or key on demand rather than strictly in sequence.

records.name: Backtracking Algorithm
records.definition: A method that explores options and reverts to an earlier point when one fails, requiring the ability to look back.

records.name: Complex Grammar/Global State
records.definition: The degree to which forbidding backtracking makes complex grammars or global-state logic hard to express.

records.name: Streaming Parsers
records.definition: The ability to parse input incrementally as it streams in, without buffering the whole document.

records.name: Control-Flow-Centric Monolith
records.definition: A monolith driven by imperative control flow rather than data dependencies, so stages cannot run or scale independently.

records.name: Data Dependencies

distinctFrom.reason: Data dependencies declare what each stage needs from others, while stages are the discrete steps themselves.

records.definition: The requirement that the data each stage needs from others be declared as explicit dependencies.

records.name: Parallel/Stream Processing
records.definition: The ability to run independent stages in parallel or stream data between them as it is produced.

records.name: Stages
records.definition: The requirement that processing be decomposed into discrete stages connected by data flow.

records.name: State Coordination
records.definition: The degree to which a data-driven design must still coordinate shared state across concurrent stages.

records.name: No Hidden State
records.definition: The requirement that a processor keep no state between invocations, so each call starts afresh from what it is given.

records.name: Parallel Processing
records.definition: The ability to process many records at once because each is handled independently of the others.

records.name: Stateful Business Rules
records.definition: The degree to which rules that inherently depend on accumulated state resist a purely stateless design.

records.name: Stateful Hidden Accumulation
records.definition: Accumulating state inside a processor across records, so results depend on invisible history.

records.name: Bounded Aggregation over Unbounded Streams
records.definition: The ability to aggregate an endless stream by grouping its events into bounded windows.

records.name: Bounded State
records.definition: The degree to which processing keeps its working state within a fixed bound regardless of input size.

records.name: Event Time
records.definition: The time at which an event occurred, carried on the event and used to assign it to a window.

records.name: Late-Data Handling
records.definition: The degree to which windowing by event time must reckon with events that arrive after their window has closed.

records.name: Unbounded Accumulation
records.definition: Aggregating an endless stream into ever-growing state that eventually exhausts memory.

records.name: Parallel Branch Processing

distinctFrom.reason: Parallel branch processing fans work out, while result aggregation brings the outputs back into one.

records.definition: The ability to process independent branches of work simultaneously across workers.

records.name: Result Aggregation
records.definition: The ability to combine the outputs of parallel branches back into a single result.

records.name: Serial Item Processing
records.definition: Processing independent items one at a time in sequence, rather than in parallel.

records.name: Fitness for Purpose
records.definition: The degree to which the chosen processing model matches the latency and volume the problem needs.

records.name: Latency Requirement Clarity
records.definition: The requirement that a workload's latency and freshness needs be made explicit before a processing model is chosen.

records.name: Latency-Appropriate Processing Model
records.definition: The ability to choose batch or stream processing to match a workload's latency needs.

records.name: One-Size-Fits-All Processing
records.definition: Forcing every workload through a single processing model regardless of its latency or volume needs.

records.name: Operational Duplication
records.definition: The degree to which supporting both batch and streaming paths duplicates operational effort and code.

records.name: Fuse Passes
records.definition: A technique for combining several passes over the same data into one.

records.name: Repeated Full Scan
records.definition: A defect in which large data is scanned or materialized several times where one pass would do.

records.name: Random Access over a Stream
records.definition: A defect in which code seeks or indexes into a source that can only be read in sequence.

records.name: Look-Back Buffering
records.definition: A defect in which a whole stream is buffered so that one stage can look back or ahead.
